You have a 3-gallon jug and a 5-gallon jug. How do you measure exactly 4 gallons?
answer: Fill the 5-gallon jug. Pour from it into the 3-gallon jug until full (leaving 2 gallons in the 5-gal). Empty the 3-gal. Pour the 2 gallons into the 3-gal. Fill the 5-gal again. Pour from it into the 3-gal (which has 2 gallons) until full — exactly 1 gallon transferred, leaving exactly 4 gallons in the 5-gal jug.

question: You have 8 identical-looking balls. One weighs slightly more than the other seven. Using a balance scale (no weights), find the heavy ball in exactly two weighings.
answer: Split the balls into groups of 3, 3, and 2. Weigh group A against group B: if they balance, the heavy ball is in the leftover pair — weigh those two to find it. If one side tips, take that heavier group of three and weigh any two of them; whichever side tips (or the unweighed ball, if they balance) is the heavy one.
